newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shekel unchanged against dlr ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israel shekel unchanged against dlr ahead of CPI.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed unchanged against the dollar on Tuesday as investors remained sidelined ahead of the release of the March consumer price index (CPI), dealers said.
The CPI, to be released on Tuesday afternoon, is expected to post a rise of 0.7 percent.
"The market was very quiet today and volume was low. Investors are waiting for the release of the CPI figure and for the outcome of today's meeting," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel will meet again on Tuesday to discuss the budget defecit. Talks began on Sunday.
"If the CPI is relatively low and the government agrees to another budget cut the central bank is expected to lower its key lending rate and the dollar would start running," the dealer said.
He added that the shekel rose against the basket following the mark's decline abroad.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4030 shekels, unchanged from Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6724 shekels against 3.6761 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6957 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6909 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9630 shekels after 1.9750 on Monday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4020 shekels.
